anya: Heads-up — ran into a reproducible numerical spike on prod when routing requests to the paged-KV + fused attention path. Sequence ~1536, batch 8. Model is gpt-medium-v2 (weights bf16), but kernel auto-selected a fp16 fastpath (fused_flash_fp16_fast).

mike: Repro steps? logs? is this from canary or main? any stack traces?

anya: Canary traffic. Repro locally with the same inputs. Paste of the critical log excerpt:
```
[attn] qk_dot max=8.12e+04, exp(max) -> inf
[attn] softmax: found inf -> NaN outputs
[decode] token loop: emitting repetition, low entropy
```
So the softmax input range is huge. Downstream tokens collapse to a single token.

rahul: That smells like exponent overflow in fp16 accumulation or a lost numerically-stable reduction. We always do log-sum-exp subtract(max) in the reference kernel. Could the fused kernel be skipping that to save ops?

elliot: The fused_fp16_fast path uses a single-kernel reduction that currently accumulates in fp16 for perf. If accum is fp16 the dynamic range is tiny (E=5bits), overflow is plausible for large dot products. BF16 weights don't help if intermediate was shunted to fp16.

zhen: Kernel selection heuristics: we pick fused_fp16_fast when (seq_len <= 2048 && batch <= 16 && kv_paged==true && model_size < 10B). So for 1536 it picked fast path. It assumed numeric-safe because we saw no failures in standard evals (mostly seq<=1024).

mike: perf impact numbers from perf-bot on canary:
- fused_fp16_fast: p50=24ms, p95=68ms, mem=6.2GB
- fused_fp32_ref: p50=42ms, p95=95ms, mem=8.1GB
Observed correctness regressions only on seq > 1200 with certain sparse attention patterns.

perf-bot: Canary alert: increased token-repeat incidents by ~3.2% in region eu-west-1 for endpoints routed to fastpath (since 2026-03-08T02:14Z). p95 latency +12% for >1024 sequences when fallback hits due to NaNs.

ops: Any immediate mitigation? Rollback the heuristic?

rahul: Short-term mitigation options:
- Force accumulation to fp32 in the fused kernel (cost: +60% latency).
- Keep fastpath but clamp logits before exp: logits = min(logits, CLAMP). Danger: changes probabilities.
- Always subtract max(logits) per row before exp (numerically stable) — if current fused kernel omits that, add it.

anya: Confirmed the fused kernel skipped per-row max-subtract for some tiled/paged layout to avoid extra passes. That explains the huge values.

elliot: Adding a per-block max then a global max would fix it without full fp32 acc, maybe acceptable perf hit. We should implement a two-stage reduction using fp32 accumulators just for max/normalizer but keep matmul in fp16.

zhen: Proposal for kernel selection update:
- If kv_paged==true and seq_len > 1024 -> prefer fused_fp32_ref or fused_mixed_accum (accumulators in fp32).
- Add a guard: if max(qk) > 1e4 (runtime check) -> fallback to safe path and emit metric "attn_numeric_guard".

mike: Sounds reasonable. Add a metric and a rate-limited log so we can correlate.

ci-bot: Created CI job: eng-runtime/attn-numeric-regression with dataset (seqs 512, 1024, 1536, 2048) and random seeds; will run fused_fp16_fast vs fused_mixed_accum. Job: #4823.

anya: I ran microbenchmarks to estimate perf tradeoffs (local dev box A100):
- fused_fp16_fast: 22ms
- fused_mixed_accum (fp16 matmul + fp32 reduction): 27ms (+23%)
- fused_fp32_ref: 44ms (+100%)
Memory delta: mixed_accum +0.5GB vs fast.

rahul: Mixed_accum seems sweet spot. Implement two-stage reduction: block max in fp16 -> convert block max to fp32 accumulate global max -> subtract and compute exp in fp32-reduced domain then cast back. Need careful vectorized impl.

ops: For rollout: patch kernel, enable mixed_accum for canary traffic for seq>=1536, monitor attn_numeric_guard and token-repeat alarm. If no incidents 24h -> expand to seq>=1024. Rollback option intact.

zhen: I'll update kernel-selection table and the fastpath thresholds. Also adding a small synthetic fuzz test to our perf harness to sweep for extreme qk magnitudes.

mike: TODOs:
- Zhen: change selection heuristics + guard metric. (ETA: today)
- Elliot/Rahul: implement mixed_accum kernel and unit tests. (ETA: 48h)
- Anya: add reproducer and attach to #4823 CI job. (ETA: 4h)
- Ops: canary rollout plan and monitoring. (ETA: 6h)

anya: I'll pin the exact input that triggered the bug to the ticket. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Note: p99 impact observed when fallback rate >1% — keep an eye.

ci-bot: CI job queued. Will post results in this thread when done.

ops: Acknowledged, will prepare rollback runbook.

mike: Great sync. If anyone hits quick wins (clamp + subtract max) push the hotfix to canary first.

anya: Posting reproducer gist in thread: https://internal.gists/r/attn-repro-1843000123

elliot: FYI: check for similar patterns in our fused cross-attn tests — cross-attn has slightly different q scaling.

zhen: Will do a sweep tomorrow across models. Closing the loop here after CI/Canary.
